title: Regular Expression Matching
statement: You get a text and a pattern. In the pattern, a dot matches any one letter, and a star means zero or more copies of the symbol right before it. Decide whether the pattern matches the whole text, not just a part of it. The pattern never starts with a star.

example.caption: In c*a*b the c* is used zero times, a* eats the two a letters, and b matches b.

idea.sentence: Let dp[i][j] say whether the first i letters match the first j pattern symbols; a star cell is true if its letter is used zero times or one more copy eats the last text letter.

jargon.plain: A symbol followed by a star is one unit. It stands for zero, one or many copies of that symbol.
The first i letters of the text, or the first j symbols of the pattern. The empty prefix has length 0.

watch.inputHint: Two strings: text, then pattern. Letters, dots and stars only, and a star must follow a letter or a dot. Keep them short.

compare.unit: steps (backtracking can really grow as 2 to the power of the number of stars)

rows.name: Plain recursion
rows.note: A star splits into two branches at every text position, and the same pair of positions is solved many times.

rows.name: DP table
rows.note: Each cell is solved once. A star cell reads two other cells, a plain cell reads one.

fast.takeaway: A star is the only place the table branches, and it branches into exactly two cells already filled. That keeps the work at table size.

stages.title: Base row and column
stages.note: The empty text matches the empty pattern. A pattern like x*y* can also match the empty text, so row 0 copies the cell two columns left at every star.

stages.title: Star: two choices
stages.note: Zero copies reads the cell two columns left. One more copy needs the letter to fit and reads the cell above.

stages.title: Plain symbol
stages.note: A letter or dot must fit the text letter, and the diagonal cell must be true.

stages.title: Read the corner
stages.note: dp[m][n] covers the whole text and the whole pattern. That is the answer.

edges.title: Empty text, star pattern
edges.why: A star can use zero copies, so the pattern can vanish. This comes only from the base row.

edges.title: Empty pattern
edges.why: Column 0 is false below the corner. A non-empty text cannot match nothing.

edges.title: Star that must give back
edges.why: a* must stop one letter early so the plain a can match the last one. The zero-copies and eat-one choices cover it.

edges.title: Dot star
edges.why: A dot with a star matches any run of letters. Each cell can eat one more letter, so the T flows down the star column to the corner.

gotchas.text: A star never stands alone. It repeats the symbol before it, so the star cell looks at p[j-2], and zero copies jumps two columns left, not one.
Eating one more copy reads the cell above in the same column, dp[i-1][j], not the diagonal. The star stays in play after it eats a letter.
Fill row 0 for patterns like a*b*. Without it, an empty text with a star pattern wrongly says false, and so does any match that skips a starred prefix.
Allocate the booleans with Array.from and a fresh array per row. A bad pattern starting with a star makes dp[i][-1] undefined, so validate the pattern if the input is not trusted.
make([][]bool, m+1) leaves nil rows. Allocate each row. Indexing p[j-2] when j is 1 would panic, which is why a pattern may never start with a star.

recap.pattern: 2-D DP over text and pattern prefixes
recap.key: A star cell is true if zero copies work (dp[i][j-2]) or a fitting letter is eaten and dp[i-1][j] is true.
moves: Make an (n+1) by (m+1) table, dp[0][0] = true
Row 0: a star copies the cell two columns left
Star: zero copies, or fit and read the cell above
Plain symbol: fits and the diagonal is true. Read dp[n][m]
